daily_brief: The day's most consequential developments center on escalating humanitarian and security crises across multiple continents. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases, with health officials warning the virus may be mutating and comparing its trajectory unfavorably to the devastating 2014 West Africa outbreak [The Guardian, RFI]. In Europe, the fallout from the Ceuta migrant crisis continues as Spain reports 3,000-5,000 migrants remain in the territory following last week's unprecedented influx, while questions mount over Morocco's role and its deepening ties with Washington [BBC Europe, The Guardian, RFI]. Meta faces a landmark $942 million total penalty in New Mexico's child safety case, the largest ruling against a social media company over harm to minors [BBC, France 24, Le Monde]. A school shooting near Bangkok killed seven people including three teachers and three students, reigniting debate over Thailand's gun laws [France 24, The Hindu]. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are poised to sign a trilateral defense pact in Jeddah as regional powers recalibrate amid the ongoing Iran conflict [France 24, Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Tops 4,000 Cases as Officials Warn Virus May Be Mutating
bullets: The DRC Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has reached 4,000 confirmed cases with 1,801 deaths as of August 4, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record
Africa CDC director Dr. Jean Kaseya announced plans to study whether the virus is mutating, citing unprecedented severity of this strain
More than two-thirds of deaths are occurring in communities rather than treatment centers, complicating containment efforts
Authorities intercepted a passenger boat heading toward Kinshasa after a suspected case was reported on board, highlighting fears of spread to the 17-million-population capital

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized mutation concerns and comparisons to 2014 outbreak severity

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Focused on containment operations including the Kinshasa boat interception

top_stories.headline: Meta Ordered to Pay $942 Million Total in Landmark New Mexico Child Safety Ruling
bullets: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million for creating a 'public nuisance' through harm to children, on top of a $375 million jury verdict from March
Judge Bryan Biedscheid compared Meta to a polluting factory, ordering the funds placed in an abatement fund to reduce future harms
This represents the largest child safety ruling against a social media company in US history
Meta announced it will appeal both rulings, stating it works hard to keep people safe and has been transparent about challenges

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Led with the 'public nuisance' framing and factory pollution analogy

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized this as part of broader state litigation against Meta

sources.name: Le Monde

top_stories.headline: Thousands of Migrants Remain in Ceuta as Spain-Morocco Tensions Persist
bullets: Between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants remain in the Spanish territory of Ceuta following last week's arrival of approximately 78,000 people from Morocco
Ceuta's leader told the European Parliament that 100 deaths occurred during the crisis and criticized Spain's national government response as late and insufficient
New calls for mass crossings are circulating on Moroccan social media, raising concerns of further influxes
Observers suggest Morocco may have orchestrated the crisis to earn favor with the Trump administration, which has deepened ties with Rabat including support on Western Sahara

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Focused on EU tensions and criticism of Spanish government response

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized US-Morocco relationship and questioned whether crisis was engineered to benefit Washington

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Highlighted broader US-Morocco rapprochement including Western Sahara and potential support for Morocco's claims on Ceuta and Melilla

top_stories.headline: Seven Killed in School Shooting Near Bangkok as Thailand Faces Gun Violence Questions
bullets: A teenage student killed his grandparents at home before shooting three teachers and three students at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, then died at the scene
The gunman fired 26 rounds using his grandfather's handgun; 34 additional rounds were found at the scene
Fifteen students were injured while fleeing; the school had approximately 3,100 students enrolled
Thailand has an estimated 10 million firearms in circulation, one for every seven inhabitants, and recent pledges to tighten gun laws have not prevented repeated shootings

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed account and highlighted Thailand's high gun ownership rates

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Offered live updates and referenced previous school shooting in February 2026

top_stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan to Sign Trilateral Defense Pact in Jeddah
bullets: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman will meet Turkish President Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Sharif to sign a joint defense agreement on Friday
The pact comes as regional powers seek to strengthen security ties amid the ongoing Iran conflict and disrupted shipping through Hormuz and Red Sea
Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir accompanied Sharif to the kingdom
Yemen's Houthis killed at least 58 Saudi-backed government troops in missile and drone attacks on Thursday, upending a 2022 truce

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Provided context on Houthi attacks and Yemen civil war escalation

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Characterized the visit as routine while noting it is Erdogan's second Saudi trip this year
